cards.explanation: The answer is honor. The LORD says, "A son honors his father, and a servant his master." He starts with something every person already understands, and then turns it on the priests. When your own example is that easy to follow, friends, it's hard to dodge the question. (Malachi 1:6)

The answer is defiled. The LORD says the priests present "…defiled food on My altar." Then the priests ask, "How have we defiled You?" and He answers that they say the table of the LORD is contemptible. (Malachi 1:7)

The answer is True. The LORD says they've defiled Him "By saying that the table of the LORD is contemptible." So it wasn't only what they put on the altar, friends. It was also what they said about it. (Malachi 1:7)

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Try offering them to your governor!" Then He asks, "Would he be pleased with you or show you favor?" It's like showing up to your boss's party with a busted lamp and calling it a gift. (Malachi 1:8)

The answer is useless. The LORD says He wishes someone would shut the doors "…so that you would no longer kindle useless fires on My altar!" Fires that should mean something are going to waste. I'd say that's a heavy thing to hear, friends. (Malachi 1:10)

The answer is False. The LORD says, "I take no pleasure in you…" and "…I will accept no offering from your hands." So these offerings aren't getting through. Better to shut the doors than keep lighting fires He won't accept. (Malachi 1:10)

The answer is nations. The LORD says, "…My name will be great among the nations, from where the sun rises to where it sets." That's a much bigger picture than one temple, bakers. Pure offerings will be presented in His name in every place. (Malachi 1:11)

The answer is that they turn up their nose at it. The LORD says, "…you turn up your nose at it…" (Malachi 1:13). The priests are looking at the LORD's table like it's something they'd rather not deal with. I think that's a lot of attitude for a table that belongs to the LORD, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "You bring offerings that are stolen, lame, or sick!" So the list gets longer than just hurt animals, friends. Then He asks, "Should I accept these from your hands?" (Malachi 1:13)

The answer is a defective animal. The man has an acceptable male in his flock and vows to give it. Then he "…sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord." The LORD calls that man a deceiver, friends. (Malachi 1:14)

The answer is King. The LORD says, "For I am a great King…" and "…My name is to be feared among the nations." That follows the curse on the deceiver, bakers. The One being cheated is the great King. (Malachi 1:14)

The answer is blessings. The LORD says, "I will send a curse among you, and I will curse your blessings." That's a serious one, friends. Their blessings are named right there in the curse. (Malachi 2:2)

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Yes, I have already begun to curse them, because you are not taking it to heart." So this isn't only a warning about later, bakers. It has already started. (Malachi 2:2)

The answer is that he stood in awe of His name. The LORD says the covenant "…called for reverence, and he revered Me and stood in awe of My name." Levi answered the covenant with reverence, friends. That is what it called for. (Malachi 2:5)
The answer is False. The LORD says of Levi, "True instruction was in his mouth, and nothing false was found on his lips." And he "…turned many from iniquity." Many, friends, not a few. (Malachi 2:6)

The answer is that he is the messenger of the LORD of Hosts. The LORD says, "…people should seek instruction from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the LORD of Hosts." That's the reason the verse gives, bakers. The priest is called the messenger of the LORD of Hosts. (Malachi 2:7)

The answer is stumble. The LORD says, "…you have departed from the way, and your instruction has caused many to stumble." Two things are named there, friends. The priests departed from the way, and their instruction caused many to stumble. (Malachi 2:8)
The answer is False. The LORD says, "You have violated the covenant of Levi…" Right before that He says they "…have departed from the way…" So no, friends, they haven't kept it. (Malachi 2:8)

The answer is partiality. The LORD says they "…have not kept My ways, but have shown partiality in matters of the law." In matters of the law, they showed partiality, friends. That's a long way from Levi, of whom the LORD says, "…nothing false was found on his lips." (Malachi 2:9, 2:6)
